title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is experiencing a mix of cautious optimism and strategic maneuvering, with new satellite approvals and significant funding allocations. Meanwhile, the hiring landscape remains a balancing act between ambition and tradition.

themes.title: Funding for Space Resilience
themes.body: The recent FY27 budget markup adds $1.4 billion to the space resilience line, signaling a strong commitment to bolstering national security in orbit. This funding could enhance capabilities against rising global threats, particularly from state actors.

themes.title: Commercial Space Consortiums Emerge
themes.body: China's unveiling of a state-backed commercial space consortium indicates a strategic shift towards consolidating resources and expertise in the space sector. This move may bolster China's competitive edge in both commercial and defense-related space activities.

themes.title: Earth Observation Sales Surge
themes.body: Earth observation satellites have overtaken telecom in European space industry sales, highlighting a growing demand for data-driven insights. This trend suggests a pivot in market priorities, as nations and businesses increasingly rely on satellite data for decision-making.

themes.title: Defense-Tech IPOs on the Horizon
themes.body: The defense-tech IPO window appears to be cracking open, with companies like Palantir securing substantial extensions on contracts. This could signal a shift in investor interest towards firms that combine traditional defense capabilities with innovative technologies.
